question: Does the growth experiment gate promote a technique to a skill ONLY when it beats the organ's sealed baseline on the sealed metric, by at least the sealed margin, at or above the sealed sample size, and clears the sealed significance in the sealed direction — judged by the Analyst from the data alone, never by who proposed it — and is every dropped technique kept on the record with its data?
why: Simon's growth-organs spec (2026-11-01). §2 HOW AN ORGAN LEARNS: baseline → hypothesis → sealed test (metric, sample size, comparison method, minimum improvement, written before running) → run → VERDICT by the Analyst (not the proposing organ) → PROMOTE (a versioned skill) or DROP (kept on record). §6 G1: every playbook entry links a passed experiment with its data. The whole point: a technique becomes a skill only after it proves itself on OUR own numbers; outside 'guru' advice is a hypothesis to test, never a rule. This kernel is that gate — pure, total, deterministic, witness-gated — the Analyst organ's verdict engine.

design.where: A kernel in this public repo, src/experiment.mjs, carrying no channel secrets and no account data. A sealed test and its measured result are plain numbers (counts and samples the organ collected from Simon's own analytics); nothing here fetches, posts or stores a credential.
design.sealedTest: A technique's test, written BEFORE it runs: { id, channel, technique, metric, kind: 'rate'|'mean', baseline (the organ's current measured level), direction: 'higher'|'lower', minImprovement (the smallest lift that is worth a skill, as an absolute delta on the metric), minSample (per arm), alpha (the significance the organ will accept, e.g. 0.05) }. normalizeTest refuses a test missing or malforming any field, with a reason.
design.result: What the run actually measured, tied to a sealed test by id: for a rate, { testId, control: {n, hits}, variant: {n, hits}, proposer? }; for a mean, { testId, control: {values:[…]}, variant: {values:[…]}, proposer? }. The proposer field is recorded but MUST NOT change the verdict.
design.statistic: rate → two-proportion z-test; mean → Welch's t with a normal approximation to the p-value (documented as an approximation, conservative for small n). p is two-sided unless the test is one-directional, then one-sided in the sealed direction. The normal CDF uses an Abramowitz–Stegun erf approximation (deterministic, |error| < 1.5e-7).
design.verdict: verdict(test, result) → { decision, improvement, stat, p, why }. INSUFFICIENT when either arm's sample < minSample (cannot conclude — keep running or drop, never promote). Otherwise PROMOTE iff improvement is in the sealed direction AND improvement >= minImprovement AND p <= alpha; else DROP. The function reads only (test, result); the proposer cannot move it.
design.playbook: promote(playbook, test, result) → on PROMOTE, a new playbook with the technique as a versioned entry { technique, channel, metric, version, testId, data (the counts/sample sizes and the computed stat/p), receipt } — its receipt is the SHA-256 of the canonical (test,result,verdict); on anything else the playbook's skills are unchanged and the failure is appended to playbook.log with its verdict and data. So no playbook entry exists without a passed experiment and its numbers (G1).
design.hardRules: The kernel decides promotion only; it never posts, never fetches, never judges engagement as real or fake (that is the auditor's and Simon's job) and carries no earnings or crypto wording. It is the measurement, not the mouth.

corpus.generator: tools/growth1-corpus.mjs, seed 20261101 — a battery of sealed tests and measured results spanning the decision surface: clear wins (big lift, significant, enough sample), near-misses (lift below margin), false lifts (big observed lift that is NOT significant), wrong-direction moves, under-sampled runs, and ties; rate and mean kinds.

claims.claim: A test must be whole and a result must match it: of 120 malformed sealed tests (each missing or malforming one field) all are refused with a reason; of 120 results whose testId names no sealed test, or whose arms are malformed, all are refused; 60 whole test+result pairs are all accepted.
claims.pass: 120 of 120 refused, 120 of 120 refused, 60 of 60 accepted

claims.claim: The sample gate holds: for every case whose observed lift >= margin and p <= alpha but either arm's sample < minSample, the decision is INSUFFICIENT, never PROMOTE.
The margin gate holds: for every well-sampled, significant case whose lift is below the sealed minImprovement, the decision is DROP, never PROMOTE.

The significance gate holds (the anti-guru core): for every well-sampled case whose observed lift >= margin but p > alpha, the decision is DROP, never PROMOTE — a big-looking lift that is not significant is not a skill.
Direction holds: a move against the sealed direction is DROP however large or significant.

PROMOTE only when all four hold: over the 400-case battery, every PROMOTE satisfies sample>=minSample AND lift>=minImprovement AND p<=alpha AND right direction, each re-checked independently in the measure; and every case that satisfies all four is PROMOTE.
claims.pass: PROMOTE set equals the independent all-four set, both ways

claims.claim: Playbook provenance (G1): promote() adds a versioned entry ONLY on PROMOTE, carrying the test id, the data, and a receipt SHA; across the battery the number of skill entries equals the number of PROMOTE verdicts, every entry's receipt re-derives from its (test,result,verdict), and every non-PROMOTE is on playbook.log; no entry lacks a passed experiment.
claims.pass: entries == PROMOTEs; all receipts re-derive; all non-PROMOTEs logged

claims.claim: Total and deterministic: 3,000 fuzzed inputs (wrong types, missing and extra fields, NaN/Infinity/huge counts, hits>n, negative n) raise nothing — each is refused with a reason or yields a verdict that reads back; and the same input gives the same verdict and the same receipt id every time.
claims.pass: 0 throws; all handled; byte-identical on repeat

claims.claim: The Analyst judges from the data, not the proposer: for every case, changing only the result.proposer field (to each persona, to 'simon', to absent) leaves decision, improvement, stat, p and receipt identical.
claims.pass: verdict and receipt unchanged across every proposer

notProven: This seals the GATE's logic, not that any particular technique helps our real audience (that is each channel organ's own sealed test on live analytics, run later), nor the significance test's exact tail beyond the documented normal approximation, nor anything about posting, platform rules or engagement authenticity (the auditor and Simon own those).
